definition: Regulation, supervision or mandatory standard is presented as a reason for action or reporting.
include_when: Document links a process, investment, data collection or report to CSRD, ESRS, taxonomy, banking or sector regulation.
exclude_when: Regulation is listed only in a glossary without connection to action.
example: CSRD readiness project; report integrated into the annual report because of CSRD.

definition: Investor, lender, customer or market expectation influences the agenda.
include_when: A stakeholder demand is linked to target selection, product, financing, rating or disclosure.
exclude_when: Generic statement that stakeholders are important.
example: Investor interest influenced KPI design.

definition: Parent group, owner or controlling shareholder shapes ESG policy or targets.
include_when: The report attributes commitments, standards or restructuring to group governance.
exclude_when: Group name appears only in company description.
example: Targets reset after separation from a former group framework.

definition: Action is justified by cost, resilience, safety, reliability, efficiency or core operational performance.
include_when: Document connects ESG action to operating costs, efficiency, security or continuity.
exclude_when: Only moral or reputational language is used.
example: Server upgrades are selected for energy efficiency.

definition: Action or disclosure is linked to trust, reputation, public acceptance or stakeholder confidence.
include_when: Document explicitly frames transparency, rating or social licence as a benefit.
exclude_when: Any public communication is not automatically coded.
example: Rating is used to provide investors with evidence of sustainability efforts.

definition: A process identifies impact materiality and financial materiality.
include_when: Methods, thresholds, stakeholders, value-chain boundaries or validation are described.
exclude_when: The words double materiality appear without process detail.
example: Management validates material IROs after scoring.

definition: A material topic is connected to how the company creates value or to its core products and services.
include_when: The report explains why the topic matters to the sector or business model.
exclude_when: A topic is merely listed as material.
example: Financed emissions are linked to the lending portfolio.

definition: Stakeholder engagement informs materiality, strategy or priorities.
include_when: The report identifies stakeholder group, engagement channel and use of input.
exclude_when: A stakeholder list has no described influence.
example: External council discusses risks with the board.

definition: Board or supervisory body has an explicit sustainability oversight role.
include_when: Responsibility, reporting cadence, approval or evaluation is stated.
exclude_when: Board members are merely named.
example: ESG status is presented to the board twice a year.

definition: A named function or executive owns the ESG agenda.
include_when: Role and authority are described.
exclude_when: A spokesperson is quoted without responsibility.
example: Board member performs the Chief Sustainability Officer function.

definition: A dedicated ESG or sustainability committee coordinates decisions.
include_when: Membership, mandate or meeting frequency is provided.
exclude_when: A committee is named without any role.
example: Committee chaired by CEO reviews targets quarterly.

definition: The organisation specifies how often performance or risks are reviewed.
include_when: Quarterly, annual or other regular review is linked to a body or KPI.
exclude_when: A one-off meeting without recurring process.
example: Strategic KPIs are evaluated quarterly.

definition: Controls, lines of defence, audit, due diligence or corrective action are described.
include_when: The mechanism can change or verify action.
exclude_when: General promise to comply.
example: Risk and compliance functions form the second line of defence.

definition: The report describes sustainability expertise, training or external advice for governance bodies.
include_when: Expertise is tied to ability to oversee or decide.
exclude_when: General employee awareness campaign only.
example: External Sustainability Council advises the Board of Management.

definition: Sustainability affects investment plan or capital expenditure.
include_when: A target or taxonomy assessment is linked to CapEx approval or portfolio.
exclude_when: The report lists green projects without capital-allocation link.
example: Transition plan is approved through the business and investment plan.

definition: Sustainability affects operating budget or recurring resource allocation.
include_when: OpEx is assigned or classified with a decision mechanism.
exclude_when: One-off donation with no governance link.
example: Taxonomy-aligned OpEx is measured for decision use.

definition: ESG information changes risk identification, limits, pricing, underwriting or mitigation.
include_when: A risk process, matrix, control or decision is described.
exclude_when: Risk is mentioned generically.
example: Climate data are incorporated into underwriting and collateral valuation.

definition: ESG performance affects variable compensation or evaluation.
include_when: Weight, KPI, target or assessment process is stated.
exclude_when: Remuneration is described but has no ESG link.
example: Board ESG KPIs materially affect variable remuneration.

definition: ESG shapes the product, service or financed portfolio.
include_when: Design, eligibility, exclusion, target or portfolio shift is described.
exclude_when: A product is called sustainable without criteria.
example: Low-emission vehicle development covers the product life cycle.

definition: ESG criteria affect supplier selection, monitoring or purchasing.
include_when: A-rating, audit, due diligence or procurement programme is used.
exclude_when: A supplier code exists without evidence of application.
example: Top suppliers are enrolled in a sustainable procurement programme.

definition: ESG metrics influence operations, maintenance or process design.
include_when: The report links a metric to concrete operational change.
exclude_when: Activity is described without decision or process.
example: Energy efficiency is required in data-centre upgrades.

definition: Metric has a baseline, target value and target year.
include_when: At least a comparable base and time-bound target are stated.
exclude_when: An aspiration lacks a baseline or date.
example: Emission intensity is to decline by more than 50% by 2030 from 2019.

definition: Comparable values are shown across multiple periods.
include_when: At least two periods use a sufficiently consistent boundary.
exclude_when: A single current value.
example: Scope 1–3 emissions are shown for 2022–2024.

definition: Organisational or methodological boundary is explained.
include_when: Entities, scopes, calculation method or exclusions are stated.
exclude_when: Metric label alone.
example: Historical data were recalculated after a method change.

definition: Metric records activity or immediate output rather than downstream effect.
include_when: Counts of participants, projects, suppliers, training or funds are reported.
exclude_when: A validated change in condition or behaviour.
example: Number of people trained in digital literacy.

definition: Metric records a change in operational, social or environmental condition.
include_when: Reduction, rate, intensity or measured result is stated.
exclude_when: Input or activity count only.
example: Water use per manufactured vehicle declined by 39.9% since 2010.

definition: Document attributes a broader societal or environmental effect to action.
include_when: Causal or contribution language about downstream impact is used.
exclude_when: Operational output with no broader attribution.
example: Programme is said to improve community quality of life.

definition: The report explicitly describes a material actual or potential adverse impact.
include_when: Negative effect, affected group, horizon or persistence is described.
exclude_when: Generic risk disclaimer.
example: Coal mining is described as having a permanent negative biodiversity impact.

definition: A disclosed KPI worsens or moves away from target.
include_when: Current value is less favourable than the comparator.
exclude_when: The report gives no comparator.
example: Scope 1+2 emissions increased year on year.

definition: The report admits a missing target, incomplete data or unavailable information.
include_when: A limitation is explicit.
exclude_when: Analyst merely infers that detail is missing.
example: No outcome-driven target exists for financed emissions.

definition: A target, boundary or method is reset, cancelled or restated.
include_when: Reason and affected metric are identifiable.
exclude_when: Routine annual update with no effect on comparability.
example: Historical carbon data were restated; group restructuring triggered target reset.

definition: Competing objectives or costs are acknowledged.
include_when: The document discusses competitiveness, affordability, reliability or transition costs against ESG aims.
exclude_when: Generic claim that sustainability creates value.
example: ESG ambition is explicitly balanced against competitiveness.

definition: An independent practitioner provides limited assurance over specified disclosures.
include_when: Scope and standard of assurance are identifiable.
exclude_when: Internal audit or an award.
example: ISAE 3000 limited assurance over the sustainability statement.

definition: Independent reasonable assurance covers a specified metric or disclosure.
include_when: The report explicitly states reasonable assurance.
exclude_when: Limited assurance.
example: Financed-emission calculation verified with reasonable assurance.

definition: The organisation states that the report was not externally assured.
include_when: Explicit non-assurance statement.
exclude_when: No assurance report is visible but absence is not stated.
example: O2 ESG Report 2024 was not externally assured.

definition: Statement is attributed to the reporting organisation and not independently verified by this study.
include_when: Most narrative claims in corporate reports.
exclude_when: Externally sourced legal fact or independently assured result within scope.
example: The company states that a programme generated positive change.

definition: Meaning is constructed by the analyst rather than directly stated.
include_when: Cross-case pattern, typology or inferred gap.
exclude_when: Neutral paraphrase of the document.
example: Decision integration is stronger where targets are tied to capital allocation.

definition: Value statement or commitment without a concrete mechanism.
include_when: No owner, metric, activity or decision link.
exclude_when: Concrete project or target.
example: Sustainability is a main priority.

definition: Specific action or output is disclosed but management mechanism or outcome remains weak.
include_when: Project, training, supplier engagement or donation count.
exclude_when: Time-bound result with governance and decision link.
example: Two hundred suppliers were engaged.

definition: Target, owner, process, method or monitored result is sufficiently specified.
include_when: At least two of target, owner, cadence, method, time series or correction are present.
exclude_when: A decision-allocation link is directly demonstrated.
example: Metric has baseline, target year and annual progress.

definition: Sustainability demonstrably affects allocation, risk, product, procurement or reward.
include_when: A formal decision mechanism is explicit.
exclude_when: Strategic priority without actual decision link.
example: ESG KPI changes variable remuneration.

definition: Specific result has a clear boundary and method plus strong independent verification or triangulation.
include_when: Assurance scope covers the metric and the claim does not exceed what was assured.
exclude_when: Assurance exists only for the report generally or causality is unproven.
example: A defined emissions metric is independently verified with reasonable assurance.
